fields.meta_title: Resume Landing Page Builder for Job Seekers | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a resume landing page from a prompt. See four job-search examples: recruiter messages, agency inquiries, a tracker, and tailored pages.
fields.h1: Build a Resume Landing Page That Gets Recruiters to Write Back
fields.hero_description: Build a resume landing page from one prompt, with your best result up top and every recruiter message in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Behind Your Resume
fields.features_subheading: A resume landing page is a one-page site that gets your resume read and makes it easy for a recruiter to contact you.
fields.feature_1:
Built from the job you want

Tell Emergent the role you want, your strongest results, and how a recruiter should reach you. It builds the page, the contact form, and the table behind them in one pass.
fields.feature_2:
Recruiter messages in a database you own

The app saves each message with the sender's name, company, role, and the link they used. That list stays yours to keep after the search ends, whichever offer you accept.
fields.feature_3:
A form that asks the right questions

Recruiters fill in the company, the role, the pay range, and a start date before they hit send. You read a complete inquiry instead of trading three emails for the basics.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts when an inquiry cannot wait

Set the rule that matters to you, such as a close start date or a named company, and the app sends you an email or in-app alert at once. The rest can wait for a weekly digest.
fields.feature_5:
Your name as the web address

Emergent includes custom domains, and they use credits. Publish the page on one made from your own name, and the link printed on your resume reads cleanly and is easy to type.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to GitHub

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans, and keep the page running wherever you host it next. The free tier covers building and publishing the page.

faq_plan.q: What is a resume landing page?
How do I create a resume landing page?

plan.angle: The searches here land on template galleries and design showcases, so the searcher wants the finished page, not theory. This page shows four job seekers whose resume landing page does a job after the click, each built from a prompt: a software engineer whose page saves every recruiter message with the link it came from, a travel nurse whose inquiry form emails her at once when a start date is close, a recent graduate whose inquiries file into a tracker with statuses, and a career changer who publishes a tailored version per application and counts replies by version. It stays on the job search: galleries of work belong to the portfolio page and the broad about-me page to personal. The FAQ covers the definition, the build, one page or a site, the first screen, recruiter contact, an own domain, projects, alerts, per-application versions and where to share the link.
tab_stories: Teo Marchetti's resume landing page saves every recruiter message with the link it arrived through, and of his 31 March messages, 19 came through the links on his applications and 12 through his profile bio link.

Marisol Vega's inquiry form asks each staffing agency for a start date, and a date within 3 weeks is emailed to her at once, so 6 of September's 21 inquiries reached her the same hour and 15 waited for the Friday digest.
Owen Fitch's page sends every recruiter inquiry into a tracker with a status, and of the 12 inquiries in his first month, 4 reached Interview, 7 sat at Replied, and 1 stayed New.
Ingrid Halvorsen publishes a tailored version of her page for each application, each with its own link, and the Analytics-led version brought 9 of her 14 replies while the Content-led one brought 5.
